params.body:
# Why

Car-Pass has a test environment (`https://ws-professionals.beta.car-pass.be/api/`) and we have De Backer's beta login, but staging could not reach it. The endpoint was a constant on `CarpassController` with the beta url commented out beneath it:

```php
const CarpassUrl = 'https://ws-professionals.car-pass.be/api/';
//const CarpassUrl = 'https://ws-professionals.beta.car-pass.be/api/';
```

An edit you have to make to test is an edit you can never merge, so staging talked to the real Car-Pass or to nothing. On top of that, staging runs on a copy of the production database, so the per-dealer `carpass_username` / `carpass_password` it carries are the *production* credentials. Registering with those against beta is wrong, and registering with them against production from staging is worse.

# What changed

**One resolver.** `App\Support\CarpassHttp` is now the only place that knows which Car-Pass answers and as whom. The constant and the commented-out line are gone; every caller goes through `CarpassHttp::url()` / `CarpassHttp::forDealer()` / `CarpassHttp::credentials()`: `CarpassController`, `CarpassSmoke`, `IntegrationSmoke`, `forceUpdateCarPass` and `VehicleApiService::updateCarpassInit`. `git grep CarpassUrl` and `car-pass.be` over `app/`, `resources/`, `tests/` and `config/` turn up no other reader (the remaining hits are `public.car-pass.be` report links, which are data, not an endpoint).

**The endpoint (`CARPASS_URL`) is a normal setting in every environment, production included.** The documented default in `config/services.php` is the production web service, so an environment that sets nothing behaves exactly as today. Pointing somewhere else must not need a deploy, and a wrong address fails loudly rather than silently.

**The credentials override (`CARPASS_USERNAME` / `CARPASS_PASSWORD`) applies only outside production.** On production the per-dealer values from the dealers table always win, whatever an env file contains. The two halves are gated differently on purpose: a single filled credential on production would make every dealer register at Car-Pass under one account, which is a real-world mess to unwind, and copying a staging `.env` onto production is a real accident. The endpoint carries no such risk. Outside production the override only applies when **both** keys are set; a username without a password falls back to the dealer record rather than sending a blank password (that only gets the account locked). The account we authenticate as is also the `enteredOrganisation` we send, so beta registrations are entered under the beta account.

**A guard for the one dangerous value.** This box is staging today and production tomorrow. A `CARPASS_URL` left on beta would keep registering politely into the test environment: Car-Pass answers, the vehicle gets a report, and none of it counts. So when the app runs as production and the configured endpoint is not the production web service, `CarpassHttp::endpointIsSafe()` is false: the platform refuses the call with that reason on screen and in the log, `stocklist:carpass-smoke` stops, and `stocklist:smoke carpass` reports a **failure** (red, exit 1), not a skip. The check sits next to the resolver, so every caller inherits it. Together with the explicit key in every env file, this replaces an environment gate on the URL: the configuration is readable, and the one value you must not leave behind cannot be left behind quietly.

**Ordering.** The registration guards sit *after* the ownership check in `carpassRequest()`, not before it. Placed first they would have turned another dealer's vehicle from a 403 into a polite 200; `RowActionsOwnershipTest` caught exactly that during the work.

# How the seal still protects

Car-Pass was **not** in `Outbound::services()` at all; it is added now, in the **impact** half. There is no innocent read at Car-Pass: every call registers an observation and is invoiced, status and report polls included. Consequences:

- outside production, nothing leaves until `carpass` is in `OUTBOUND_IMPACT`. `CARPASS_URL` pointing at beta opens nothing: the address says *where*, the impact list says *whether*;
- `CarpassController::carpassRequest()` asks `Outbound::impact('carpass')` explicitly and returns the reason to the dealer instead of letting the HTTP seal throw a 500;
- the seal only opens the configured base url (`<CARPASS_URL>/*`) for a service in `OUTBOUND_IMPACT`;
- the demo stays closed regardless, as before.

`stocklist:smoke carpass` now prints, before anything else on the line: which Car-Pass (production / test environment (beta) / own address) with its host, whether the account comes from the environment or from the dealer record, and whether the seal is open. Never a username-password pair, never a password. That line matters tomorrow.

# What Shane must set on staging

```
CARPASS_URL=https://ws-professionals.beta.car-pass.be/api/
CARPASS_USERNAME=<the beta account from Car-Pass>
CARPASS_PASSWORD=<its password>
OUTBOUND_IMPACT=...,carpass
```

The beta environment needs **its own** credentials from Car-Pass; the ones in the database are production. And on production, per `CUTOVER.md`: set `CARPASS_URL` explicitly to `https://ws-professionals.car-pass.be/api/` in the same step where `APP_ENV=production`, so the env file itself says which Car-Pass the platform uses. Forget it and `php artisan stocklist:smoke --all` goes red immediately, so run that as the first command after the switch. The two credential keys are ignored on production by design; leaving them behind is harmless.

# Follow-up, not in this PR

`FLEXLEASE_URL`, `REAL_GARANT_API_URL` and `BLURIT_URL` are listed in `.env.example` but empty, and their `config/` entries have no default at all, so neither the env file nor the config says which endpoint those integrations use. Same fragility as the one fixed here, and worth the same treatment; not the day before the cutover.

# Checked

- `php artisan test --filter='Carpass|CarPass|Outbound|IntegrationSmoke|SmokeTest'`: green. Full suite green too, apart from `BuildStampTest` which reads the checkout's build stamp and fails in any worktree.
- New `tests/Feature/CarpassEndpointTest.php` (16 tests): the config default is production; the setting decides the endpoint the HTTP client is given (asserted on the url, with `Http::fake()`), on production as well; outside production the env credentials win and are sent as Basic auth and as `enteredOrganisation`; without them the dealer's own are used; a half-filled override falls back to the dealer; on production the env credentials are ignored while the endpoint still follows the setting; the beta url alone does not open the seal (nothing sent, no allowed pattern) while `carpass` in `OUTBOUND_IMPACT` does; production against beta refuses and the smoke line is a failure with exit 1; production against production proceeds; beta outside production is fine; the smoke line names endpoint, source and seal and never prints a password.
- `docs/bedrijfsregels/13-s3-car-pass.md`: R S3-1.7 (endpoint per environment, production the default), R S3-1.8 (credential override, production ignores it), R S3-1.9 (production refuses a non-production endpoint) and R S3-7.5 (what the smoke line says), with R S3-1.5 and R S3-1.6 corrected. `92-testdekking.md` and `docs/bedrijfsregels.html` regenerated with `bin/rules-coverage --write` and `bin/rules-page`.
- Rebased on `main` after #305; the only conflicts were the two generated rule files, regenerated from the merged chapters.
- No real credential in any test or in `.env.example` (placeholders only).
params.title: Car-Pass: point staging at the test environment
